ArXiv cs.AI.description:

Abstract: This research involved the study of an application of Case-Based Reasoning (CBR) in the field of academic advising. Academic advisement has been recognised as an important function of higher education. However, there is a widespread desire to improve the advisement services provided by many educational institutions (e.g., colleges and universities) around the world. ArXiv cs.AI.title: NormGym: Evaluating Normative Competence through Social Interaction
ArXiv cs.AI.description:
arXiv:2611.08613v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Normative competence, the ability to infer socially enforced expectations from interaction and adjust behavior accordingly, is essential for agents operating in unfamiliar human communities. Yet existing evaluations largely test whether agents can recognize or apply norms they may already know, rather than whether they can acquire previously unknown norms from social interaction. We introduce NormGym, an interactive benchmark for normative competence in which a newcomer must infer a hidden, arbitrary norm while pursuing its own task in a multi-a

ArXiv cs.AI.description:
arXiv:2611.08626v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: E-commerce supply chains generate large volumes of customer feedback and operational data that remain underutilized in inventory management. Traditional inventory classification techniques such as ABC analysis rely primarily on annual dollar usage, while multi-criteria inventory classification (MCIC) methods extend this but still depend on structured quantitative data and do not utilize unstructured information available in modern supply chains. ArXiv cs.AI.title: Aspect-wise Pairwise Tournaments for Test-Time Selection
ArXiv cs.AI.description:
arXiv:2611.08640v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Scaling test-time compute has proven highly effective at improving LLM reasoning. A popular method is best-of-n sampling, where a model generates many candidate solutions and one is selected. This motivates the question: how can we select the best candidate? When humans make choices, we find it more natural to compare two options than judge each in isolation. ArXiv cs.AI.title: Decision Context: Persistent Behavioral Learning for AI Agents
ArXiv cs.AI.description:
arXiv:2611.08644v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: LLM agents do not learn from corrections across sessions. A user fixes the same mistake at the start of every conversation. Existing agent memory systems primarily handle facts, such as preferences, entities, and conversational history, rather than procedural knowledge.
  We present Forge Decision Context (forge_dc), a system that captures behavioral signals from human corrections and self-assessed tool-call failures, compiles them into imperative RULE directives, and injects them at the decision points where they apply. We evaluate forge_dc alo

ArXiv cs.AI.title: IWIBench: Evaluating Gradient-Free Model Driven Intra-weight Injection
ArXiv cs.AI.description:
arXiv:2611.08647v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Intra-weight injection lets one model change another model's behaviour by editing its weights directly, without gradients. Such edits can range from altering lexical associations to enforcing output formats or updating factual knowledge. Despite growing interest in these approaches, there has been no systematic way to evaluate how well models perform them. ArXiv cs.AI.description:
arXiv:2611.08666v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Interactive debuggers are indispensable to human software development, yet coding agents overwhelmingly rely on edit-execute-observe loops, using common bash tools, test scripts, and print statements to debug via repeated shell commands. Stepping through a debugger provides live access to runtime state, which may enable different problem-solving capabilities. However, prior work typically introduces the debugger as an additional tool or through a new subagent, making its individual contribution difficult to isolate from the associated scaffold c

ArXiv cs.AI.title: ChainFlow: Few-Step Latent Flow Matching for Speculative Decoding
ArXiv cs.AI.description:
arXiv:2611.08669v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Speculative decoding has become a standard way to accelerate LLM inference: a lightweight drafter proposes tokens that the target verifies in one parallel pass. Existing drafters face trade-offs that limits their speedups: autoregressive drafters generate tokens one at a time, so drafting cost grows with draft length, while diffusion drafters generate tokens in parallel but predict each position independently, ignoring inter-token dependencies. ArXiv cs.AI.title: Transporting the Past: An Optimal Transport View of Backtracking Counterfactuals
ArXiv cs.AI.description:
arXiv:2611.08682v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We study backtracking counterfactual inference for Structural Causal Models (SCMs) through the lens of optimal transport. In SCMs, a factual observation generally induces a posterior distribution over exogenous variables, making counterfactual inference inherently distributional. We introduce two complementary frameworks that transport this posterior onto the set of exogenous configurations satisfying a desired counterfactual query. ArXiv cs.AI.title: Cancellation Is Not Enough: What Retries Leave Behind in an Overloaded LLM Engine
ArXiv cs.AI.description:
arXiv:2611.08684v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Clients and proxies in front of an LLM engine retry calls that time out. After a transient overload, these retries can keep the engine from recovering even when calls arrive below its capacity. Since the engine may keep computing for clients that have left, propagating cancellation looks like the natural remedy. In this paper, we test it on vLLM with overload experiments on three open models, and with scheduler traces of one that follow each client attempt to the execution it creates in the engine. ArXiv cs.AI.title: Memory-Aware Multi-Agent Architecture with LLM-based Orchestration for Conversational Recommendation
ArXiv cs.AI.description:
arXiv:2611.08718v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Conversational recommender systems often treat user sessions in isolation, limiting their ability to capture how user intent evolves over time. While large language models (LLMs) have improved semantic understanding, they are typically used as isolated components, without addressing how memory, retrieval, and decision-making should be integrated at the system level. ArXiv cs.AI.title: AlterNet: Adaptive-Depth Mixture-of-Experts with Learned Halting for Elastic Inference
ArXiv cs.AI.description:
arXiv:2611.08741v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Most LLM architectures have fixed compute demands determined at training time. We propose a novel architecture that combines the Mixture-of-Experts architecture with shallow experts and a novel dynamic-depth system to make the extent of a forward pass dynamically adjustable. Our approach lets the model automatically determine the compute needed for a given task, paired with a system to scale it down after training without retraining when the execution environment demands faster or cheaper inference. ArXiv cs.AI.title: AttentionSwitch: Jailbreak Defense for LLMs via Joint Learning of Sparse Attention-Head Selection and Scaling
ArXiv cs.AI.description:
arXiv:2611.08752v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Large language models have achieved remarkable performance across a wide range of tasks, yet they remain susceptible to jailbreak attacks that circumvent safety mechanisms and elicit harmful or unintended outputs. Although safety can be improved through model fine-tuning, such approaches can be computationally expensive and may degrade previously acquired capabilities through catastrophic forgetting. ArXiv cs.AI.title: Debate to Deceive: Poisoning LLM's Fact-Checking via Game-Theoretic Multi-Agent Debate
ArXiv cs.AI.description:
arXiv:2611.08756v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Knowledge attacks on Large Language Models, such as manipulating fact-checking judgments, pose significant risks to AI reliability. Existing approaches -- adversarial suffix/template injection and single-agent self-reflection -- lack robustness across diverse defenses and are prone to confirmation bias and costly trial-and-error, respectively. ArXiv cs.AI.title: Jacobian-Causal Memory Control for Persistent Memory in Language Model Systems
ArXiv cs.AI.description:
